title: SafeShell Raw Linux Command Schema
description: Schema for raw Linux/Bash command examples before parsing, semantic enrichment, context collection, and risk/intent labeling.

id.description: Unique identifier for the command example.

command.description: Complete raw Linux/Bash command exactly as represented in the source example.

category.description: Broad functional category of the command.

subcategory.description: More specific operation performed by the command.

commands.description: Command/program names appearing in the command. Useful for pipelines and chained commands.

flags.description: Options or flags appearing in the command.

arguments.description: Arguments, paths, values, patterns, filenames, or other operands supplied to commands.

operators.description: Shell operators present in the command.

redirections.description: Input/output redirection operators present in the command.

has_sudo.description: Whether sudo appears in the command.

has_pipe.description: Whether the command contains a pipeline.

has_redirection.description: Whether the command contains input/output redirection.

has_chaining.description: Whether multiple commands are chained using shell operators.

has_command_substitution.description: Whether command substitution such as $(command) or backticks is present.

has_variable_assignment.description: Whether the command contains shell variable assignments.

has_glob.description: Whether wildcard/glob patterns such as *, ?, or [] are present.

has_shell_expansion.description: Whether shell expansion constructs are present.

has_subshell.description: Whether a subshell construct such as (...) is present.

execution_mode.description: Whether the command is intended to execute in the foreground or background.

target_types.description: Types of resources explicitly targeted by the command, when identifiable from the command itself.

paths.description: File or directory paths explicitly present in the command.

environment_variables.description: Environment variables referenced or assigned in the command.

description.description: Human-readable description of what the command is intended to do.

name.description: Name of the source, dataset, documentation, or contributor.

reference.description: Source reference, URL, document identifier, or other provenance information.

license.description: License information associated with the source, when known.

tags.description: Additional descriptive tags such as destructive, privileged, network, recursive, or administrative.
